material.description: Stated request (commit d302127): recall reports index convergence; partial digests resume. Possible real problem: memory_sync budgets (memory_sync.*_budget_ms) are smaller than one full sync pass, so each dispatch restarts from the same point and the index never converges; reporting convergence only makes the stall visible. Check: record the partial digest across repeated dispatches and whether its cursor advances. Witness: two consecutive recall replies showing the cursor or processed-count moving forward.

material.description: Stated request (commit 5f11f1e): bump rs-plugkit for the allowOutsideRoot ancestor grant. Possible real problem: the dispatch cwd resolves to a directory whose git toplevel differs from the project the caller meant (a submodule or a nested repo), so the grant lets an out-of-root path through instead of correcting the root. Check: for each caller that triggered the grant, compare the cwd, the git toplevel and the .gm directory it resolved to. Witness: one dispatch from a submodule cwd through the real verb showing which .gm tree it read or wrote.
material.title: XY check: allowOutsideRoot ancestor grant may hide a wrong project root
material.witness: REFUTED. The grant does not re-root: the refused read from cwd rs-plugkit names root C:\dev\gm\rs-plugkit (dispatch 1791850569252-500-598ef7b534462833, out-file rs-plugkit/.gm/exec-spool/out/fs_read-...-1791850560085-130.json); the opt-in read of C:/dev/gm/AGENTS.md is ok under the same root (dispatch 1791850572034-500-b7bf1ea5075a8267). The dispatch was made from a submodule cwd, so it is in rs-plugkit's ledger, not this project's; the binding is the four-field form, whose exit code 0 means the probe ran to a reply, not that the verb returned ok. callers outside_root_read_granted -> project_path_rejection only. Witness-log line appended. Residual gap (success reply has no root echo) filed as XY-ALLOWOUTSIDEROOT-SUCCESS-NO-ROOT-ECHO (1791850821209-500-b44aa29965964e69). Receipts .gm/receipts/XY-ALLOWOUTSIDEROOT-MASKS-WRONG-ROOT/01-08.

material.description: Ubiquitous Language (P2). The word pin means a submodule pin in AGENTS.md and scripts/triage/check-pins.sh, but gm-mcp/src uses bare pin for a different thing, the sha256 local-build pin (cli.js:163-170 pin-local-build and unpin-local-build with locals pin and pinPath; release-bridge.js:17 RUNNER_PIN_FILE). The self-update module already says LOCAL_BUILD_PIN_FILE, localBuildPinPath and pinLocalBuild. Change in scope gm-mcp/src/cli.js and gm-mcp/src/release-bridge.js: rename the bare pin and pinPath locals to localBuildPin and localBuildPinPath, and RUNNER_PIN_FILE to RUNNER_LOCAL_BUILD_PIN_FILE, so the code always carries the qualifier the submodule meaning lacks. On-disk file names are unchanged. Witness: grep for bare pin or pinPath identifiers in gm-mcp/src/cli.js returns none, and gm-mcp/src/cli.js self-update-status still prints the local_build_pin_path key.

material.description: Ubiquitous Language (P2). Suppressing automatic bundle/runner updates is named no-self-update in the on-disk marker and env (NO_SELF_UPDATE_FILE 'gm-mcp-server.no-self-update' and RUNNER_FREEZE_FILE 'agentplug-runner.no-self-update', GM_MCP_NO_SELF_UPDATE and RUNNER_FREEZE_ENV), in AGENTS.md, and in the self-update verb name. The code names the same concept freeze: selfUpdateFreezeReason and bridgeFreezeReason in gm-mcp/src/self-update.js:48 and gm-mcp/src/release-bridge.js:164, the frozen locals at self-update.js:219 and release-bridge.js:294, and the frozen_by / 'freeze state' output in self-update.js:153 and cli.js:218. Decision recorded: no-self-update is the ubiquitous term because it names the marker and env the operator types. Change: rename the code identifiers to noSelfUpdate* (selfUpdateFreezeReason -> selfUpdateSuppressedReason is NOT the choice; use noSelfUpdateReason, bridgeNoSelfUpdateReason, and frozen -> suppressed) in gm-mcp/src/self-update.js, gm-mcp/src/release-bridge.js and the cli.js help and status text. The wire field frozen_by is a user-visible output key and is NOT renamed here; that choice is a mutable for the user. Witness: grep for freeze in gm-mcp/src returns only frozen_by, and node gm-mcp/src/cli.js self-update-status prints the same reason text as before.

material.detail: Root cause (verified live, not the shell-out hypothesis): walk_posix in rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/code_index.rs is a pure in-process walk over host_fs_readdir. On C:\dev\aloopprime, fs_readdir {"path":"."} lists an entry named `nul`, but fs_stat {"path":"./nul"} returns not-found, because nul is a reserved DOS device name Win32 will not open in any directory. With checked == true walk_posix did `return Err("file stat failed for {next}")`, propagating as file_enumeration_failed / complete:false / enumeration_complete:false -- so one unstattable entry costs the whole project its index and every codeinsight call answers 'symbol index refresh is incomplete' forever. FIX IS WRITTEN BUT NOT LANDED: committed as rs-plugkit 8395d5ebadd008c2c29810024e5a80d7f60248ab (one path, crates/plugkit-core/src/code_index.rs) -- unstattable entries are now skipped and recorded (FileEnumeration::skipped_unstattable surfaced by codeinsight_index) instead of fatal, and Windows reserved device names (con/prn/aux/nul/com1..com9/lpt1..lpt9, case-insensitive, with or without extension, plus trailing-dot/space) are pre-filtered only when the host cwd is Windows-shaped so a POSIX aux.rs still indexes. Compile-verified: cargo build -p rs-plugkit --release --target wasm32-wasip1 --features slim exit 0 (5,656,887-byte wasm). NOT DONE: the wasm was never installed to ~/.agentplug/plugins/gm.wasm, so no live codeinsight verification ran -- reconfirmed 2026-10-10 that C:\dev\aloopprime codeinsight_index {"action":"status"} still returns complete:false / 'file stat failed for ./nul'. PUSH BLOCKED, DO NOT FORCE: rs-plugkit main is not a fast-forward of origin/main and another writer has crates/plugkit-core/src/config_sync.rs dirty with 5082 staged deletions under .agentplug-kv/codeinsight-edges/ -- pulling over that clobbers in-flight work. Landing sequence: wait for that writer, pull, push, rebuild+install gm.wasm, then re-run codeinsight_index sync and codeinsight callers on aloopprime.

material.detail: Measured 2026-10-11 on c:/dev/gm by lane aaf4e517 (row gm-config-refresh-degraded-silent-nested-copy-cause, fix committed as c0ee16ee40277855db7f87bf86d0442231e6ef4b): git_push {rev:"c0ee16ee..."} failed verbatim "push of explicit source ref 'c0ee16ee40277855db7f87bf86d0442231e6ef4b' to main failed because the remote moved ... Recover with exactly: git_pull {branch:"main"} to fast-forward past the remote's new commit, then git_push {rev:"HEAD"}", and the recovery it names then refused verbatim "worktree or index is not clean, so a pull could clobber uncommitted changes -- refusing exactly as before. Dirty tracked files: .gm/prd.yml, skills/gm-orchestrate/SKILL.md, skills/gm-prd/SKILL.md, ...". The served recovery is unreachable in the normal case: every lane keeps .gm/prd.yml dirty (rows append continuously, and a path-scoped commit cannot include it without allow_foreign_rows), so pull is refused exactly when the recovery commands it. Acceptance: on a repo whose remote moved and whose dirty set is lane-owned, the served recovery ends with the sha pushed -- either git_pull fast-forwards past a dirty set it never touches (stash/restore), or the recovery names the clean-tree step first (path-scoped git_finalize of the dirty tracked files, .gm/prd.yml with allow_foreign_rows) before the pull. Witness: on a repo with a moved remote, dirty .gm/prd.yml and one edited skill, running the served recovery verbatim ends with the sha pushed and ci-status read on it, not with a second refusal.

No README, AGENTS.md or SKILL.md text names the job, its scope (history, not only the working diff), or what must happen when the heuristic misses. Done when the job's boundary is stated, and a witness shows a seeded credential shape blocked before push.

material.body:
Claim (DBC, precondition on verb calls): arguments must satisfy the verb schema, and a call carrying keys outside the schema is refused. Witness: gm-mcp/src/codemode.js:15 validates with z.object(tool.inputSchema), which strips unknown keys by default, so a misspelled field is dropped with no error. Live check, session gm-goal-w4-DBC: codesearch with bogus_field:1 was admitted and searched; codesearch with cwd:12345 was refused ("cwd: expected string"). Type checks hold; unknown-key rejection does not. Fix is not a one-line change: .strict() would reject the session_id and cwd defaults the codemode contract forwards to verbs whose schema omits them. Needs a test on that path and a bundle rebuild (gm-mcp src and committed bundle together).

material.acceptance: (1) a version file whose content carries a leading U+FEFF is read as its semver after the BOM is stripped; (2) it is never classified as a local-dev sideload; (3) a BOM'd .version no longer freezes guest upgrades (reconcileGuest proceeds to upgrade); (4) a genuinely non-semver marker (e.g. 'dev', 'local', 'abc') still classifies as local-dev-sideload; (5) live witness (id, hash, ts) from a real dispatch reproducing the freeze with a BOM'd .version in a scratch home and never touching C:\Users\user\.agentplug, then showing fixed code reading it as semver.
material.subject: BOM'd plugins/<name>.version freezes guest upgrades as a fake local-dev sideload
material.text: Live defect 2026-10-10: C:\Users\user\.agentplug\plugins\gm.version bytes are \u{feff}0.1.1520 (leading U+FEFF). The agentplug-runner plugin-update poll refuses it as 'not recognized X.Y.Z semver' and writes gm.local-dev-sideload.json (installed_marker "\u{feff}0.1.1520"); gm-mcp/src/release-bridge.js reconcileGuest then returns {outcome:'skipped', reason:'local-dev-sideload'}, so gm.wasm is never upgraded from AnEntrypoint/plugkit-bin again. Live daemon stuck on 0.1.1520 while plugkit-bin is at 0.1.1539, silently. Same silent-BOM class as row gm-reverify-silent-on-unparsable-prd (spoint orch b186): a BOM turns a live upgrade path into a permanent silent no-op mislabelled as an intentional developer sideload. Fix at source on BOTH the Rust runner (agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/download.rs) and the JS bridge (gm-mcp/src/release-bridge.js, gm-mcp/src/self-update.js, anything reading .version): strip a leading U+FEFF before any semver test/compare of an installed version file. Keep real sideload detection intact: a genuinely non-semver marker stays a sideload.

material.description: Stated assumption (M1 answer, live evidence in .gm/receipts/INVEST-EARS-DOC-PATHS-EXIST/witness-gm-goal-improve-20261013T1-w1-result.md, dispatch 1791850824875-500-ea797479c05e8473): the doc-path criterion counts only slash-containing references. Bare names with no directory are excluded: 249 checked, 20 unique absent (specify.md x41, emit.md x24, update_docs.md x12, state.md, sec.md, prd.yml, mutables.yml, plugkit.wasm, gm.wasm, bert.wasm, active-strategy.json, source.json x4, p.json x4, POLARIS-SKILLS-GUIDE.md, lean-pN.md and others). Many look like served stage names rather than files. Decide: either a bare name that a doc presents as a file is also a repository path (then each must be given its directory or marked as runtime or served state), or the exclusion stands and is written into the row's criterion. Done when the row criterion states the rule and the scan reflects it. Decision (session gm-backlog-w2-70): the exclusion stands. Criterion: a repository path is a backtick or code token that starts with a shipped top-level root (scripts/check-doc-paths.mjs ROOTS); a bare file name with no directory is not checked. The scan states this rule in its header comment.

material.description: Finding (lane h2 report, 2026-10-16): an omitted cwd resolves to the gm-mcp server process cwd /workspace/office/Office. No literal 'office' or 'Office' exists in rs-plugkit (plugkit-core: 267 files, complete scan, 0 matches; rs-plugkit: 316 files on disk, 0 matches). Root resolution is cwd-driven: rs-plugkit orchestrator/mod.rs stateful_cwd_root_once() (line 87) takes the process cwd when it holds .gm; nonrepo_fallback_root (line 220) takes it verbatim otherwise. rs-plugkit cannot tell an omitted cwd from a supplied one, so an rs-plugkit-only fix would refuse every non-repo cwd and break the documented cross-repo audit root (PROJECT_ROOT_UNRESOLVABLE_WORKAROUND). The omission is decided where the gm-mcp server is launched (gm-mcp submodule, uninitialized in /workspace/gm). Fix belongs in gm-mcp dispatch (refuse, or default from the caller session, when cwd is absent) or the launch cwd; needs a scope decision before any edit.
material.subject: Blocked: omitted cwd resolves to the gm-mcp server launch directory, not a hard-coded office path
material.witness: Decision: no harness variable, no guess. resolveDispatchRoot (gm-mcp 6afa312) already refuses cwd-less calls with error cwd-required unless GM_MCP_DEFAULT_CWD or the server cwd is a git toplevel. c1380fe drops CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR from that list (the shared HTTP singleton inherits it from whichever session spawned it, pinning every later session to that project) and the stdio relay now injects its own launch cwd into a tools/call lacking cwd when that cwd is a git toplevel (launchRootDefault). Witness: relay launched in /workspace/gm, gm_codemode with no cwd ran phase-status rooted at /workspace/gm (payload /workspace/gm/.gm/exec-spool/out/phase-status-pw-gmmcp-1018-536489-*.json, dispatch 1792313000489-500-7888f77d897b37a5). CI green run 39112775650.

material.description: prd_list and prd_add dispatches sat in queued_not_yet_claimed for about 80 minutes (claim_sweep_stalled, oldest unclaimed 2541707 ms) while claim slots were free. The daemon sweep stalls the whole project. Add a sweep watchdog that restarts the claim pass when the oldest unclaimed dispatch exceeds its bound.
material.resolution: Lease verbs run off the claim pass; claim_sweep_stall watchdog (claim_sweep_stall_secs, default 300) restarts a daemon whose main loop stops advancing while requests starve.
material.subject: dispatches sit unclaimed for over an hour
material.witness: Root cause reproduced in an isolated AGENTPLUG_HOME daemon: browser_lease_acquire against a foreign-held owner.json (wait_ms 240000) ran inline in dispatch_project and blocked the main loop; health wd-6 sat unclaimed and the new watchdog logged 'claim sweep stalled: the main loop has not advanced past phase dispatch-batch for 38635 ms ... request unclaimed for 35644 ms' and exited 71 (dispatch 1792313353978-500-90b86cc2849f2ba4). With lease verbs on their own thread (agentplug 41a1c55, released 0.1.360, rust-ci + release run 39113405168/39113405154 green), a foreign-held lease wait wde-1 stays inflight while health wd-8 and wd-9 answer in 100 ms each (dispatch 1792313696110-500-a995a76651d43d3).

material.acceptance_criteria: A live dream-replay-cycle reply names candidates[] whose first entry is the incumbent policy id, carries a per-candidate replay score over the same sealed worlds, and a selected id equal to argmax with ties to the incumbent; codesearch "incumbent" in dream_cycle.rs or the function it calls returns a hit.
material.description: EARS ubiquitous: the system shall score the incumbent pi^0 and M-1 challengers by replay and redeploy the argmax. Event-driven: when a cycle boundary is reached, dream-replay-cycle shall replay the candidate set. Gap: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/orchestrator/dream_cycle.rs:41 calls dream_rsi::automatic_replay, which (dream_rsi.rs:769-780) sums per-dispatch quality and picks "replay-recorded-successes-first" if any score==0.0 else "continue-current-exploration". No policy set, no incumbent id, no per-candidate score, no argmax, so the paper monotonic guarantee (never worse on replay) is unenforced. The sealed-world incumbent-vs-challenger engine exists (dream_rsi.rs:1315-1384, dream-replay-round with policy_id/world_id/beta1/beta2) and skills/dream-rsi/references/dream-rsi.md:15 claims incumbent stays unless a challenger scores strictly higher, but the cycle trigger never invokes it. Evidence dispatches: 1792313037549-500-15c5d58a24689f00 (dream_cycle fns), 1792313050182-500-ff6d41b7b2322f3 (automatic_replay), 1792313065236-500-4eaae94cc69a2dca (challenger absent from code), 1792313060175-500-2cdc2acda961f361 (doc claim).

row.description: evaluate_policy (dream_rsi.rs:240-290) reads only policy.roots and policy.max_nodes; group_size, stop and attempt (parsed at lines 154-177) are never consulted during replay and only pass through to the ranking/declared output (lines 336-338, 384-386). material.description: skills/gm-hop/SKILL.md (Node emission) sets applied:true only when a change landed and witness quotes dispatch ids that skills/dream-rsi/SKILL.md Part B step 4 finds in .gm/dream-rsi/<session>/observations.json. rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/orchestrator/dream_rsi.rs:554-573 observe_dispatch returns early for prd-add, prd-resolve, prd-list, mutable-*, instruction, transition, residual-scan and dream-*. So a read-only hop (row filing is its only change, the usual case under a no-edit brief) can only quote codesearch/callers ids; the prd-add id that IS the change is never verifiable. Witnessed in walk pw-hops-1018: all five hops (JTBD, XYPROB, EARS, INVEST, THINSLICE) reported their prd-add ids absent from observations.json and quoted only search ids; my own prd-add 1792312957244-500-5f87358b29c5c16d is absent from .gm/dream-rsi/pw-hops-1018/observations.json. Fix one side: either Part B accepts ids from .gm/exec-spool/.dispatch-ledger.json (which records every verb), or observe_dispatch records prd-add/prd-resolve, or gm-hop says a row-only hop quotes the ledger id.

material.description: rs-plugkit orchestrator/dream_rsi.rs automatic_replay reads one session's observations.json, takes its last 8 rows and verifies each through dispatch_ledger::lookup, which holds only MAX_ENTRIES=500 dispatches (about 28 min of multi-agent load on 2026-10-18). Most sessions are short-lived (56 of 109 have one observation), so their history never replays: live cycles after the agentplug task-id fix answer status deferred, reason no-verified-observations (out files dream-replay-cycle-mcp-codemode-1099-...-678.json etc). Paper H_t is the whole accumulated history. Fix: aggregate observations across .gm/dream-rsi/*/observations.json by ts for a project-scope cycle, verify against the ledger or the dispatch's own out JSON (as witness binding already does), and relax the ledger session_id equality to the observation's owner. Also dispatch_ledger::record is an unlocked read-modify-write, so concurrent dispatches drop entries.
material.subject: Dream replay verifies only a 500-entry ledger window per session
material.witness: dream-replay-cycle dispatch 1792314612845-500-e5a423b059f11667 status replayed over the whole project history (167 sessions, 1525 observations, 61 worlds; dropped counted by reason: unconfirmed_by_ledger_or_spool_out 578; ledger_confirmed 261, spool_out_confirmed 686); 8 candidates incl. incumbent pi0-default, argmax pi0-default.group-4 1.0020 vs baseline 0.8948, never_worse true, contract defects []; cycle-result.json read back by fs_read 1792314623030-500-7827732d2e05c717. rs-plugkit 465166d (c735e710da), CI run 39114426332 success. ledger record() now compare-and-swaps (host_cas_write, 16 attempts).

material.description: Two gm_codemode calls whose JS body polled for 4-5 min failed with 'gm-mcp relay: HTTP server at http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp unreachable: TypeError: fetch failed' while the server stayed up. Node undici fetch has a 300 s default headersTimeout, so the relay fetch dies on long bodies. Fix in gm-mcp: a dispatcher with headersTimeout/bodyTimeout above the codemode ceiling. Also the gm_codemode tool text says prd_add takes a body field, but prd_add refuses body (declared: description).

material.description: Concurrent lanes editing the same rs-plugkit file (verbs.rs, verbs/search.rs) can only commit their own hunks by temporarily writing HEAD+own-hunks into the working file, staging, then restoring it, which races with other lanes doing the same through one shared index (seen 2026-10-18: the working verbs.rs briefly lost two lanes' hunks). A git_add/git_commit option taking a patch or hunk selector (git apply --cached) would remove the working-tree swap.
material.subject: git_commit has no hunk-level scope for files shared by concurrent lanes
material.witness: rs-plugkit 74ba797 (on origin/main via 660872b). git_commit {patch} or {hunks:{path:[n]}} builds the commit in a temp GIT_INDEX_FILE read from HEAD, applies only the named hunks, writes the tree, runs commit-tree with the configured identity, and moves HEAD by update-ref CAS. The work tree is never written. The shared index entry moves to the new blob only where it still equals the old HEAD blob; otherwise it is reported in index_left_staged. Witness (built guest under agentplug-runner dispatch, 17/17 PASS): two lanes edit one file at lines 2 and 28. hunks {f.txt:[1]} commits lane A only, the work tree stays byte-identical, HEAD omits lane B, and the remaining diff is lane B's hunk alone. A patch built from that diff commits lane B, after which nothing is modified or staged. Refused: an out-of-range hunk (the reply lists the hunk count), a patch that does not match HEAD (stage apply), and an .agentplug path.

The work tree is never written. The shared index entry moves to the new blob only where it still equals the old HEAD blob; otherwise it is reported in index_left_staged. Witness (built guest under agentplug-runner dispatch, 17/17 PASS): two lanes edit one file at lines 2 and 28. hunks {f.txt:[1]} commits lane A only, the work tree stays byte-identical, HEAD omits lane B, and the remaining diff is lane B's hunk alone. A patch built from that diff commits lane B, after which nothing is modified or staged. Refused: an out-of-range hunk (the reply lists the hunk count), a patch that does not match HEAD (stage apply), and an .agentplug path.

material.description: After git_add {paths:[...]} staged exactly 5 files, git_commit without paths refused with blanket_stage_refused naming the same 5 paths. When the index equals what this session staged via git_add, commit it without requiring paths again.
material.subject: git_commit ignores paths staged by git_add
material.witness: rs-plugkit 74ba797. git_add records each session's staged paths in kv git_add_staged: the previous record intersected with what is still staged, plus this call's paths. An unscoped git_commit skips the blanket_stage refusal when the index equals that session's record, and commits the index as staged. Witness (same file): git_add {paths:[h1.txt,h2.txt], session_id:lane-S}, then git_commit {message, session_id:lane-S} with an untracked junk.txt present: committed true, HEAD carries h1.txt, junk.txt not committed. Negative: lane-S stages k.txt and lane-T stages m.txt; lane-S's unscoped git_commit is refused, so another session's staging is never swept in.

material.description: skills/gm-hop/SKILL.md (Node emission) tells a hop to stamp lean_node on its dispatches; rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/wasm_dispatch/verbs.rs:3065 reads body.lean_node into observe_dispatch. So no observation can ever carry lean_node, and Dream-RSI Part B per-node attribution (dream_rsi.rs:1925 record.get('lean_node')) is always empty. Fix: add lean_node to VERB_OWNED_RESERVED_BODY_KEYS-style envelope handling (strip before validation, keep for observe_dispatch) in rs-plugkit and accept it as a top-level envelope key in gm-mcp.

acceptance_criteria: evaluate_worlds refuses a non-finite beta1, beta2, policy score or baseline_score with a named error
live dream-replay dispatch with a world producing NaN quality returns ok:false, not improved:false
material.description: Precondition gap. dream_rsi.rs:280 replay_score = quality - beta1*cost + beta2*parallelism_bonus, and :323-327 averages it with no is_finite check (other inputs are filtered at :126,:192,:1074). If baseline_score is NaN, the filter at :355-361 (score > baseline_score) is false for every candidate, so the incumbent is returned with improved:false and no error; a NaN candidate is likewise dropped via unwrap_or/partial_cmp Equal at :362-367. never-worse then holds vacuously and hides a broken scorer. beta1/beta2 are also unchecked for finiteness.
material.subject: evaluate_worlds has no finiteness precondition on scores: a NaN incumbent silently disables every candidate
material.witness: Repro before fix: dispatch 1792319010848-500-c4140318fdd41688 returned ok:true with replay_score null and improved:false (baseline_score -0.0, beta1=beta2=1e308, 2 observed nodes). material.description: Independence-Based Verification: skills/gm-validate/SKILL.md:15 forbids the executor session witnessing its own edit (verifier runs as <parent>-v<k>), and lean-p3.md:117 (G_INDEP) requires a fresh verifier session given only the contract. skills/gm-hop/SKILL.md:35 lets the hop set applied:true and pick its own witness_dispatch_ids; the only check is Part B id presence. No lane that did not produce the change re-runs the witness. Specify in gm-hop/gm-orchestrate: when a hop emits applied:true with a source change, the orchestrator spawns a verify lane (session <hop>-v1) that is given the node file changes and witness pointers only, re-dispatches the witness verb, and stamps verified_by:<session> on the node file; Part B counts applied only with verified_by != node session. Distinct from gm-hop-row-witness-unobservable (rows as the landed change).

material.acceptance_criteria: write_claim_heartbeat writes <marker>.tmp.<pid> then renames over the marker, matching claim_dispatch.rs:513-514.
material.description: Fallacy: the network/filesystem is reliable. claim_dispatch.rs:793-800 write_claim_heartbeat uses fs::write (truncate then write), violating the AGENTS.md rule that guard markers use atomic create or rename. claim_heartbeat (:802-808) parses pid\nts; a read between truncate and write returns None and the orphan sweep judges the claim on age alone (the message at :798 admits this path), so a live long dispatch can be swept as orphaned.

material.acceptance_criteria: Two concurrent dispatch-driven daemon starts that each record a wasted start leave wasted_starts equal to 2 in daemon-spawn-backoff.json. A live witness: dispatch-verb selfcheck of the backoff path after a forced double start shows the count. The write goes through tmp file plus fs::rename, and a torn file is treated as unknown, not as zero.
material.description: [repo: agentplug] What is wrong: record_wasted_daemon_start reads daemon-spawn-backoff.json, then writes wasted_starts+1 with a plain fs::write. Two daemon starts racing can both read N and both write N+1, so the backoff undercounts; a torn read returns (0,0) via unwrap_or, which silently resets the backoff to base. Where: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon.rs:727-733 (record_wasted_daemon_start) and :710-716 (read_wasted_daemon_start_backoff). Evidence: codesearch dispatch 1792317358332-500-3d4bb6677cea6591 (backoff matches at daemon.rs:702-724); fs_read dispatch 1792317366585-500-3341ee3cd779342 (daemon.rs:700-750).
material.subject: Wasted-start backoff counter is a non-atomic read-modify-write
material.witness: Two concurrent agentplug-runner daemon starts against a live owner (pid 1233115, fresh heartbeat) with a cleared daemon-spawn-backoff.json left wasted_starts=2 with ts set (file read directly after both exited). Commit 8afd1f7 on agentplug main (merged as 8aa7ea7; CI run 39121564000 success 10/10). Before the fix the RMW used a plain fs::write with no lock. Torn backoff file now reads as the ceiling window, not zero.

material.acceptance_criteria: A live fs_read dispatch of a missing relative path returns error text that names the io kind (not found) and echoes the relative path; a permission-denied path names permission denied; both witnessed by dispatch ids in the reply.
material.description: [repo: rs-plugkit] fs_read on a relative path that does not exist returns error 'file read failed' with no kind (not found, permission) and no path echoed. The catch-all arm maps every io error to one string, so the caller cannot tell a typo from a permission fault. Where: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/wasm_dispatch/verbs.rs:1040 (`_ => err("fs_read", "file read failed")`). Evidence: gm_codemode fs_read {path:"does-not-exist.md"} with cwd /workspace/gm (session rollout-9-1018) threw 'file read failed'; the same call with an absolute path threw a path-rule message, so the two failures are indistinguishable by kind.
material.resolution: rs-plugkit fs_read catch-all arm now names not-found vs unreadable cause

acceptance_criteria: A Part B run rejects a node record citing a foreign-session dispatch id
A Part B run accepts a record citing its own prd-add id and names unobservable verbs instead of rejecting silently
material.description: skills/dream-rsi/SKILL.md:33-34 counts a walk when every witness-quoted dispatch_id appears in any observation file; it never binds the id to the record session, to a write verb for applied:true, or to the node, so a hop can cite a foreign read-only codesearch id and pass. Conversely dream_rsi.rs:920-937 observe_dispatch never records instruction, prd-list, transition, mutable-* or dream-* verbs, so a hop quoting its prd-list id (gm-hop step 5 mandates prd-list) is falsely rejected; Part B never names observations-archive-*.json (grep archive in skills/dream-rsi: 0 hits) though session_history reads them. lean_node stamping is refused, so binding cannot use lean_node. Fix: step 3 reads observations.json plus observations-archive-*.json; step 4 requires ids from the record session, and applied:true requires one write-class id (git_commit, fs_write, prd-add) whose reply_sha256 re-hashes (ORACLEBIAS-pw-hop-ORACLEBIAS-1018-1); gm-hop names the unobservable verbs that must not be quoted. Witness: 1792314135283-500-6cb2c890fdd1acc0, 1792314106597-500-c22285113b2f186a.

material.description: [repo: gm-mcp] [group: gm-mcp/src/codemode.js] What is wrong: an outer gm_codemode call with max_chars 16000 ran a nested gm.prd_list that requested max_chars 200000, and the nested reply came back at reply_max_chars 6000 with reply_truncated true. material.acceptance_criteria: A live dispatch that waits reports its wait split into named phases (queue, lane, daemon) whose sum matches dispatch_waited_ms, and an exec_js child with exit_code nonzero reports top-level ok false.
material.description:
[repo: gm-mcp] [group: gm-mcp/src/dispatch.js]
What is wrong: a reply can report dispatch_waited_ms far above its own execution time, and the reply gives no split between queue, lane and daemon time. The exec_js probe reported duration_ms 35 with dispatch_waited_ms 38213 and the outer ok true even though the child exited 1, so a caller cannot tell whether the time was spent in the queue, in a lane, or in the child.
Where: gm-mcp/src/dispatch.js:1974 (return { ...out, dispatch_waited_ms: waitedMs }).
Evidence: dispatch 1792321113363-500-5228a338bf372aa3 (exec_js, duration_ms 35, exit_code 1, dispatch_waited_ms 38213, top-level ok true); dispatch 1792321004822-500-97c0a0947c4e08b7 (codesearch, dispatch_waited_ms 12237).
material.subject: dispatch_waited_ms has no breakdown of where the wait sat
material.witness: gm-mcp/src/dispatch.js withDispatchWait adds dispatch_wait_split {admission_ms, unattributed_ms} summing to dispatch_waited_ms. Live witness on the rebuilt bundle (node bin/gm-mcp-server.js dispatch exec_js, 6 s body, cwd /workspace/gm): dispatch_waited_ms 7401 = admission_ms 0 + unattributed_ms 7401. Commit d6a0ac3cd99f4fb9dcb8813f488dd332819f8e4a pushed to gm-mcp main. Acceptance clause 2 (exec_js exit_code nonzero gives ok false) lives outside this file and is filed as find9-exec-exit-nonzero-ok-true. Queue and lane are not separated: the daemon reports only admission_waited_ms.

material.description: [repo: gm-mcp] [group: gm-mcp/src/cli.js] What is wrong: when a CLI command fails, the wrapper prints only the command name and error.message. It names no dispatch id, no spill file and no log path, so a failed run cannot be traced to its dispatch from the output. Where: gm-mcp/src/cli.js:380 (console.error of `gm-mcp: ${command} failed: ${error.message}`). Evidence: the same file prints dispatch-free errors at lines 241 and 260, while gm-mcp/src/codemode.js:53 already builds the dispatch_id form the CLI omits.
material.resolution: Already fixed upstream in 1435235; verified live, no new commit required.

material.description: Repro: content = await gm.fs_read({path}) returns a dispatch envelope (dispatch_id, verb, '--- data (verbatim, no indentation added) ---' header) and gm.fs_write({path, content}) writes that whole string back, prepending the envelope to the file. Observed on AGENTS.md (dispatch 1792322610666-500-7b0d77a0fc40a97e, restored by git_checkout). Fix direction: fs_read returns the raw data string for scripted use, or fs_write refuses content that starts with a dispatch envelope header. Also seen: gm-mcp HTTP relay at 127.0.0.1:8787 dropped twice mid-session (fetch failed), recovered with node ~/.gm-tools/gm-mcp-server.mjs ensure-http.

material.acceptance_criteria: With GM_CODEMODE_TIMEOUT_MS unset, a gm_codemode body that awaits a never-returning call returns the deadline error text before the harness limit; a live dispatch witnesses it.
material.description:
[repo: gm-mcp] [group: gm-mcp/src/codemode.js]
What is wrong: DEFAULT_CODEMODE_TIMEOUT_MS is 600000, the same as the harness tool-call max. The in-process deadline therefore cannot fire before the harness kills the call, so the 'did not finish within' message with resume guidance is never returned to the caller. This is plausible and not yet witnessed.
Where: gm-mcp/src/codemode.js:18 and :22-29.
Evidence: source read via codesearch dispatch 1792321037722-500-65a54b6548ee390b; the prd-add describe reply shows the timeout ceiling of 600.
Fix direction: default the codemode deadline below the harness ceiling (for example 540 s) so the resume hint is returned.
material.subject: gm_codemode default deadline (600 s) equals the harness max
material.witness: Live witness, GM_CODEMODE_TIMEOUT_MS unset: a body that awaited a real prd-list dispatch (1792332808641-500-6d516bc94f0aeff1) and then a never-returning promise threw 'gm_codemode code did not finish within 540000 ms' after about 539 s, under the 600 s harness limit (codemode-1719554-1792333347727-289). codemode.js:18 defaults to 540000 at HEAD 22d19aa6885d2e115c6247149ebb618c3ea9c3e6; CI green (run 39133253446, 4 of 4 jobs success). Residual 600000 constants in spool-transport.js and stdio-relay.js filed as find4-codemode-deadline-budget-constants.

material.description: exec_js 1792314655671-500-4d31bb11e8e44440: 764 tracked files incl. INDEX.md, du 3.0M. codesearch prd-superseded in rs-plugkit/crates = 0 hits (1792314666141-500-28606b6bea9ae88f); sole writer is skills/gm-finish/SKILL.md:10 ("Archive title-only row files into .gm/prd-superseded/ with an index line"). An agent hand-moves files and hand-edits INDEX.md: no CAS, no hash chain, unbounded growth in git. Resolved rows already move material into .gm/prd-log.jsonl via append_chained. material.acceptance_criteria: Witness: a wasm-plugin-release run with build started before bump finishes (ci-status job timestamps), and the released wasm sha matches a build of the bumped tree (sha256 in release-assets).
material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml]
What is wrong: release needs bump, and bump commits and pushes the version before build starts, so the wasm build (cold for each asset key) is strictly after plan and bump. The version is a Cargo.toml string, so the build could run on the pre-bump head and the bump could be applied after with no code change.
Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml: jobs plan, bump, release (needs: [plan, bump]); build step in release
Evidence: fs_read of rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml in session find-10-1018
material.subject: wasm release builds only after the bump commit, plan->bump->build serial
material.witness: Release run 39135865193 (release -> publish/release -> wasm-plugin-release.yml) on sha 51fc62ceb1: step 'Commit and push the version bump before the build starts' completed 14:25:10Z and step 'Build' started 14:25:10Z, Build finished 14:25:44Z, Publish release succeeded. Pre-fix order (bump push after Build) reproduced by fs_read dispatch 1792333379801-500-e242a17eded38d63. Post-fix live ordering witness: codesearch dispatch 1792333419799-500-638ed9407ac6a529 (commit/push step line 135 before Build line 150). CI on sha 51fc62c: 8 of 8 jobs success (ci-status dispatch 1792334375259-500-1b9f192a332193d6). Secrets check RESULT: PASS. Note: the row's 'needs: [plan, bump]' description is stale; there is no bump job, the bump now precedes Build inside release.

material.acceptance_criteria: A skill-release run whose push is rejected because main moved retries on the new base and publishes; witnessed by a workflow run id whose log shows the retry line. Or the push is replaced with the bump-pins retry loop shape.
material.description: [repo: gm] .github/workflows/skill-release.yml 'Auto-bump patch version' step runs `git push origin HEAD:main` once, with no fetch/rebase and no retry. The workflow concurrency group only serialises skill-release runs, not bump-pins or human pushes to main, so a push that lands between checkout and push fails the release after the bump is computed. Evidence: fs_read dispatch 1792317332552-500-af02bdf059c2a807.

material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml]
What is wrong: doc-drift checks out gm-config and rs-plugkit in full on every push and PR, then runs scan-doc-drift, check-doc-counts, check-doc-paths and check-graph-traversal serially in one job. check-doc-counts also runs inside gh-pages, so the same work repeats.
Where: .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml:9-30; scripts/check-doc-counts.mjs is repeated at .github/workflows/gh-pages.yml build step
Evidence: fs_read of .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml and gh-pages.yml in session find-10-1018
material.subject: doc-drift runs four gates serially and clones two repos per run
material.witness: Already fixed on main, no edit needed. doc-drift.yml runs scan, doc-counts, doc-paths and graph-traversal as separate jobs that each need only the changes gate (commit 3362313a), and the changes job skips all of them on an irrelevant change, so gm-config and rs-plugkit are not cloned then. gh-pages.yml has no check-doc-counts step (commit 067384311b, 'gh-pages: drop duplicate check-doc-counts step'); codesearch for check-doc-counts shows only doc-drift.yml. ci-status for sha 647acd5c6f07f9cb0711642076cc0410fbb76159 (doc-drift commit, descendant of 3362313a): 9/9 jobs success, run_status success, run https://github.com/AnEntrypoint/gm/actions/runs/39137691236. Remaining note: scan clones three repos (gm-config, rs-plugkit, gm-mcp) and each other gate clones two; these are required by the gates, not duplicates.

material.description: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/orchestrator/dream_rsi.rs read_observation_values returns Vec::new() for a leading-'[' file that fails to parse (serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Value>>(raw).unwrap_or_default()) and silently skips unparseable JSONL lines (filter_map(.ok())). session_history and automatic_replay therefore see fewer records with no reject count. The write path does not erase data: observe_dispatch appends, and rotate_observations_if_full archives the raw bytes before a compare-and-swap truncate (witness 1792324924345-500-6268fb0d4ed4cf4c shows a malformed '[{' seed preserved byte-for-byte in observations-archive-1792324917992.json). The original row claim of overwrite-erasure does not reproduce.

material.acceptance_criteria: Live dispatch: with a lock file whose mtime is older than LOCK_STALE, two concurrent record_wasted_daemon_start calls (exercised through the runner selfcheck or a spawn-loop probe) leave wasted_starts equal to the number of calls. A held lock past LOCK_WAIT still increments wasted_starts or logs a named refusal, never a silent drop. Witness: daemon-spawn-backoff.json shows the expected count in the dispatch reply.
material.description: [repo: agentplug] [group: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon.rs] What is wrong: with_wasted_daemon_start_lock (daemon.rs:725-756) breaks a stale lock by checking its mtime and then calling remove_file, with no re-check. Two processes that both observe the same stale lock can each remove the lock, and the second remove deletes a lock the first just created, so two writers enter the critical section and one wasted_starts increment is lost. Separately, when LOCK_WAIT (2 s) expires the function returns at daemon.rs:739-740 without running critical, so record_wasted_daemon_start silently drops the record and the exponential backoff (daemon.rs:797-799) never grows for that start. Where: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon.rs:742-752 (stale break), :739-740 (timeout return), :758-774 (record). Evidence: codesearch regex over agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon.rs for backoff|BACKOFF|sleep( in session find-5-1018 (dispatch id in the truncated reply), plus the Read of daemon.rs:706-800 in this session.
material.subject: Spawn-backoff lock stale-break is check-then-remove, and a timed-out write is dropped
material.witness: Commit 2ac80e594d437daba293bd70f2f3160cb778ea0a on agentplug main (pushed, git_push remote_sha matches). Stale-break now renames the lock to a pid-suffixed parked file, re-checks its age, restores it with hard_link only if still fresh, then removes it. Lock-wait timeout now runs the critical section with an eprintln refusal instead of returning silently. cargo check -p agentplug-runner passes (only a pre-existing deprecation warning at daemon.rs:2278). Live witness is the compile dispatch; the two-process stale-race probe in acceptance_criteria was not run in this session.

material.acceptance_criteria: No @v<n> or branch-ref action use remains in gm/.github/workflows or gm-mcp/.github/workflows; every uses: line carries a 40-character commit sha.
material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: .github/workflows/contracts.yml]
Wrong: contracts.yml:13 and :16 use actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-node@v4 (tag refs). doc-drift.yml, bump-pins.yml and skill-release.yml pin full SHAs (11d5960..., fbc6f39...), and gm-mcp/.github/workflows/verify.yml also uses @v4. Mixed pinning means a moved tag changes CI silently, and the same action resolves to two versions across workflows.
Where: .github/workflows/contracts.yml:13,16; gm-mcp/.github/workflows/verify.yml (checkout and setup-node steps).
Evidence: codesearch '@v4' dispatch 1792343633130-500-6924c9e81b79e084; fs_read of bump-pins.yml 1792343587622-500-6b8ffc8cea0bd3d6, skill-release.yml 1792343588690-500-1260d7983f0dcb31, doc-drift.yml 1792343589632-500-c6b60a195fe228ab.
Acceptance: codesearch 'uses: actions/' over .github/workflows and gm-mcp/.github/workflows returns only @<40-hex-sha> refs, witnessed by a dispatch id.
material.subject: workflows mix SHA-pinned and @v4 action refs
material.witness: contracts.yml now pins actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 and actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 (the SHAs other workflows already use). Post-edit codesearch regex over contracts.yml shows 2 hits, both 40-char SHAs, no @v4. Pushed as d559ff85e487beed6a3f2893343c01d3f49c14ab. Other files (doc-drift, bump-pins, gm-mcp verify.yml @v4) left for a follow-up row.

material.acceptance_criteria: gate_ok returns non-zero when the matching run count is zero for the target tip; a bump run on such a tip prints held and stages no pin.
material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: scripts/bump-pins.sh]
Wrong: gate_ok (scripts/bump-pins.sh:12-16) counts only non-green release|publish|build|wasm runs. If the submodule tip has no such run yet (queued late or not created), pending=0 and the gate opens, so the pin advances to an untested tip. The spec in AGENTS.md says an unreadable gate holds, but a zero-run answer is treated as green.
Where: scripts/bump-pins.sh:12-16 (gate_ok), :32 (caller).
Evidence: codesearch 'gate_ok' dispatch 1792343638962-500-2bcf27026b616734; fs_read of bump-pins.sh (dispatch 1792343600779-500-b9a97bb8bc96ce58).
Acceptance: for a tip with zero matching runs, gate_ok returns held, and a live bump-pins run logs 'held <path>' instead of advancing.
material.subject: bump-pins gate passes when a tip has no release-path runs yet
material.witness: Commit df6657d048 (on origin/main) changes gate_ok in scripts/bump-pins.sh so a zero-run answer is 'none' and holds. Live exec_js dispatch 1792344092233-500-1e1e62557a9fc503 runs the edited gate_ok against a stubbed gh: zero runs -> GATE_HELD, one green release run -> GATE_OPEN, one queued build run -> GATE_HELD. Pre-edit run (same method, git-free) returned GATE_OPEN for zero runs. bash -n passes.

row.subject: download.rs has no windows-aarch64 runner asset mapping
row.witness: No edit needed: agentplug HEAD 2ac80e594d437daba293bd70f2f3160cb778ea0a (clean tree, origin/main) already maps (windows, aarch64) to agentplug-runner-windows-arm64.exe at download.rs:1128 and asserts it in runner_asset_matrix_accepts_only_published_host_targets at download.rs:2700-2705. codesearch 'windows-arm64' in download.rs returns 2 hits (lines 1128, 2704).

material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: install.sh]
What is wrong: the MINGW/MSYS/CYGWIN arch case maps only x86_64 to agentplug-runner-windows-x64.exe, so an ARM64 Git Bash host falls through to the FATAL 'no published agentplug-runner binary' exit, although install.ps1 and the runner publish windows-arm64.exe.
Where: install.sh:34 (case arm), install.sh:410 (FATAL message).
Evidence: dispatch 1792343599378-500-5d3651e36d872763 (install.sh arch case lines 15-34, uname -m mapping, no windows arm64); dispatch 1792343611762-500-7b40c32921e90c81 (install.ps1:18 ARM64 arm exists).
acceptance_criteria: codesearch for 'windows-arm64' in install.sh returns a hit inside the windows arch case; a live install dispatch under an ARM64 MSYS uname selects windows-arm64.exe instead of reaching the FATAL line.
material.subject: install.sh windows branch accepts only x86_64 under MSYS
material.witness: install.sh detect_asset now maps aarch64|arm64 under MINGW*/MSYS*/CYGWIN to agentplug-runner-windows-arm64.exe (matches install.ps1 ARM64 and download.rs windows aarch64). Live bash dispatch stubbed uname for aarch64, arm64 and x86_64 and sourced detect_asset: outputs windows-arm64.exe, windows-arm64.exe, windows-x64.exe; bash -n install.sh SYNTAX_OK. Committed f406ed45 and pushed to origin main.

The wasip3 build (cargo +nightly build -p rs-plugkit --release --target wasm32-wasip3 --features slim,wit-env, EXIT=0) imports gm:plugkit/env@0.1.0 (23 of 24 funcs; host-vec-search unused) and wasi 0.3 interfaces, and exports nothing. material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml]
What is wrong: no workflow runs npm audit or cargo audit or cargo deny. doc-drift.yml installs gm-mcp with --no-audit, which skips the advisory check entirely. A codesearch of the workflows for audit found only that one line. Advisories against pinned zod, js-yaml, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, esbuild or Cargo crates would not block a release.
Where: .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml:59.
Evidence: codesearch literal 'audit' over .github dispatch 1792343717215-500-48e648a6181f61d8 (1 hit, line 59); codesearch regex 'cargo audit|npm audit|cargo deny' over repo dispatch returned 0 hits with scan INCOMPLETE, so the zero is not a finding by itself.
Acceptance criteria: (1) a workflow file exists under .github/workflows that runs npm audit --omit=dev for gm-mcp and cargo audit for rs-plugkit and agentplug; (2) a live codesearch literal 'cargo audit' over .github returns at least one hit; (3) the job is green on main, cited by run id.
material.subject: No dependency audit gate in CI for npm or cargo trees
material.witness: Edit in .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml adds 'npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high --prefix gm-mcp' after the install step in the scan job; pushed as acf6e8a6987fd77d0f42da778e9b7ab16ca292d7 on main. Live witness: the exact step command exits 0 against gm-mcp (dispatch 1792344810701-500-5cf976345b0f5325). Scope note: the cargo audit half (rs-plugkit, agentplug) is filed as find12-cargo-audit-gate. CI not awaited per row instruction.

material.acceptance_criteria: Live dispatch witness: with two dispatches racing on a stale gm.db.lock, exactly one holder exists after settle (owner record names the surviving pid), and the removed-lock path renames the lock to a parked name and re-reads the owner record before deleting, with its reply naming the parked path. Verify by exec_js reading .gm/gm.db.lock.owner after the race; dispatch ids recorded in the receipt.
material.description:
[repo: agentplug] [group: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon/claim_dispatch.rs]
What is wrong: settle_store_lock reads the owner record, decides the lock is stale (dead pid or heartbeat older than STORE_LOCK_STALE_MS), then calls reclaim_store_lock, which runs remove_dir(lock_dir) or remove_dir_all(lock_dir) and remove_file(owner_file) with no re-read of the owner record in between and no atomic rename-away step. A second daemon can reclaim and re-acquire the lock in that window, and the first daemon then deletes the second daemon's live lock and owner record, so two writers can hold gm.db at once. Where: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon/claim_dispatch.rs:599-603 (reclaim_store_lock) and :614-660 (settle_store_lock). Evidence: fs_read of claim_dispatch.rs lines 575-674, dispatch 1792345093918-500-9064b0d02411b1f0. The write path already uses atomic rename in daemon.rs with_wasted_daemon_start_lock (daemon.rs:712-760), so the store lock is the inconsistent one. row.description:
[repo: agentplug] [group: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon/claim_dispatch.rs]
What is wrong: settle_store_lock reads the owner record, decides the lock is stale (dead pid or heartbeat older than STORE_LOCK_STALE_MS), then calls reclaim_store_lock, which runs remove_dir(lock_dir) or remove_dir_all(lock_dir) and remove_file(owner_file) with no re-read of the owner record in between and no atomic rename-away step. A second daemon can reclaim and re-acquire the lock in that window, and the first daemon then deletes the second daemon's live lock and owner record, so two writers can hold gm.db at once. Where: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon/claim_dispatch.rs:599-603 (reclaim_store_lock) and :614-660 (settle_store_lock). Evidence: fs_read of claim_dispatch.rs lines 575-674, dispatch 1792345093918-500-9064b0d02411b1f0. The write path already uses atomic rename in daemon.rs with_wasted_daemon_start_lock (daemon.rs:712-760), so the store lock is the inconsistent one. material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: .gitignore]

What is wrong: manual recovery steps left two full copies of the PRD log in the workspace root of .gm: prd-log.jsonl.prepull-find0.bak (1106525 bytes, 2026-10-18T12:56) and prd-log.jsonl.cynefin-1018-2.bak (1095542 bytes, 2026-10-18T12:13). Both are untracked, not ignored, and not pruned, and each is a full copy of a 1.35 MB live log. Each git_pull blocked by the dirty prd-log creates another copy, so SSD use grows with every workaround.

Where: .gm/prd-log.jsonl.prepull-find0.bak and .gm/prd-log.jsonl.cynefin-1018-2.bak; the git status snapshot lists both as untracked (??).

Evidence: exec_js dispatch id 1792345231061-500-e6d48c8e91b258eb (stat of both .bak files and the live log at 1349800 bytes); git_status at session start lists both paths as untracked.

Why it matters: disk and read cost on every whole-tree walk, and the backups can be mistaken for live state.

material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: scripts/check-doc-paths.mjs]
What is wrong: scripts/check-doc-paths.mjs runs only at the root. Running it inside rs-plugkit, agentplug or gm-mcp fails with Cannot find module (no per-submodule copy), so doc paths inside those submodules are never checked. At the root it reports RESULT: PASS while skipping 19 paths under uninitialised submodules (rs-codeinsight, agentplug-bert, agentplug-libsql, agentplug-treesitter, rs-search, agentplug-crux). A PASS therefore hides unchecked paths. Evidence: dispatch 1792345067778-500-e9ba572c8e9f2131 (root PASS with 19 skipped), dispatch 1792345194589-500-245ce1bde9edb29c (submodule FAIL, Cannot find module).
material.subject: check-doc-paths skips submodule docs and passes on skipped paths
material.witness: Commit 8bc69fb4d5696e0902ad442f217330c12911a011 (pushed to main). Live run of scripts/check-doc-paths.mjs at root: walks initialised submodule docs (rs-plugkit, agentplug, gm-mcp) and reports 'checked 396 repository path(s) named in 403 file(s); skipped 19 under uninitialised submodule(s)' with the six uninitialised names; it no longer prints a silent PASS. It now reports two genuine [FAIL] lines in rs-plugkit/README.md:418 and :439 (vendor/), filed as find6-rs-plugkit-readme-vendor-paths. Running it inside rs-plugkit still fails with Cannot find module (no per-submodule copy); the checker is root-only by design.

material.acceptance_criteria: After a crawl session closes and the idle window passes, the profile directory under .gm/browser-lease is at most a fixed budget (witness: exec_js du of .gm/browser-lease before and after a crawl dispatch id with close). component_crx_cache is excluded from the profile or capped (witness: a second crawl dispatch id still launches and the cache directory size stays under the cap).
material.description:
[repo: agentplug] [group: agentplug/crates/agentplug-host/src/crawl_lease.rs]

What is wrong: the Chrome profile under .gm/browser-lease/session/profile keeps 46987258 bytes. component_crx_cache alone holds about 25 MB in one 25678309-byte entry plus 7.9 MB, 2.6 MB, 1.3 MB and several 0.3 to 1 MB entries. These are Chrome component updater downloads that are re-fetched on every profile reuse. The profile also keeps a BrowserMetrics .pma (4 MB) and a History file (200 KB). Nothing in the lease path prunes this cache, so each project holds the full profile on SSD while the lease is idle.

Where: agentplug/crates/agentplug-host/src/crawl_lease.rs (profile path and lease lifecycle; the user-data-dir flag is set in crawl.rs, see agentplug/crates/agentplug-host/src/crawl.rs).

Evidence: exec_js dispatch id 1792345082506-500-bae0c57275106a08 (directory sizes, browser-lease 46987258 bytes, largest component_crx_cache file 25678309 bytes); codesearch literal user-data-dir returns crawl.rs and crawl_lease.rs.

Why it matters: SSD use per project, and cold-start time when the cache is re-downloaded.

material.acceptance_criteria: On macOS arm64 and x64, the script detects sha256sum or falls back to 'shasum -a 256' and prints 'ok: <path> (sha matches)' for an already-present verified file. On Linux the same output is produced. Live dispatch or script run on each platform is cited.
material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/scripts/fetch-weights.sh]
What is wrong: check_sha() pipes sha256sum into awk. Stock macOS ships shasum, not sha256sum, so on a Mac the check always fails. The fetch loop then re-downloads the model and fails with 'sha mismatch', so the bge model weights cannot be fetched on macOS (arm64 or x64) without a manual install of coreutils. Linux and Git Bash on Windows ship sha256sum and are unaffected.
Where: rs-plugkit/scripts/fetch-weights.sh:19 (check_sha body, sha256sum call), :54-57 (mismatch exit after re-fetch).
Evidence: codesearch for 'sha256sum' scoped to rs-plugkit/scripts/fetch-weights.sh returns the single hit at line 19 (dispatch 1792345194246-500-46130572c4c2c5c8 family of codesearch replies; no separate witness run yet).
material.subject: fetch-weights.sh needs sha256sum, absent on stock macOS
material.witness: Commit ad4978987497492e5f7a53e5d2cfc2235895a066 (pushed to rs-plugkit main as ad0b0f331fde024298703954a2acb54b154fbb72) makes check_sha use sha256sum when present and shasum -a 256 otherwise. Live dispatch 1792345869448-987 sourced the real check_sha from rs-plugkit/scripts/fetch-weights.sh with PATH excluding sha256sum: a matching file returned success and a wrong sha returned failure. Earlier dispatch 1792345641326-806 showed shasum -a 256 and sha256sum print identical hashes on this host. Not run on macOS hardware; CI reads the result.
material.witness_plan: Run rs-plugkit/scripts/fetch-weights.sh on a macOS runner with a pre-placed weights file; expect the ok line and exit 0.

material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: .gitignore]
What is wrong: rs-plugkit/.gitignore:3 ignores Cargo.lock, so the lockfile is not tracked and the Rust build resolves versions fresh each time. No rs-plugkit workflow or script passes --locked (agentplug/.github/workflows/release.yml:48 does). rs-plugkit/Cargo.lock exists on disk but is not in git.
Where: rs-plugkit/.gitignore:3; rs-plugkit/.github/workflows (absence of --locked).
Evidence: codesearch dispatch 1792345308390-500-c248fb160666d8fd (Cargo.lock hits: only .gitignore:3 and README.md:499); codesearch dispatch 1792345309231-500-7f584b7fb436d505 (--locked only in agentplug release.yml:48); fs_stat dispatch 1792345271261 family (Cargo.lock present on disk).
Acceptance: a live codesearch dispatch in rs-plugkit for literal Cargo.lock finds no .gitignore hit, and a live codesearch for --locked in rs-plugkit .github finds at least one build step; Cargo.lock is listed in git_status or tracked after the fix.
material.subject: rs-plugkit Cargo.lock is gitignored and CI never builds --locked
material.witness: Edit removed Cargo.lock from rs-plugkit/.gitignore (commit 92115ca98e, pushed to main, remote main 92115ca98e). Live witness: exec_js git check-ignore -v Cargo.lock in rs-plugkit exits 1 (not ignored). Earlier live codesearch literal Cargo.lock on rs-plugkit/.gitignore returned 0 matches. Commit identity defect filed as prd row find12-commit-identity-personal-email. CI --locked wiring is out of scope and not waited on.

material.description:
[repo: gm] [group: .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml]
What is wrong: doc-drift.yml:61 runs `npm install --prefix gm-mcp --no-audit --no-fund --ignore-scripts` instead of `npm ci`. npm install rewrites gm-mcp/package-lock.json to match package.json instead of failing, so the job never reports lock drift, and the npm audit at line 62 scans the re-resolved tree rather than the committed lock. Known drift already exists (row find12-gm-mcp-lock-drift: zod absent from the lock).
Where: .github/workflows/doc-drift.yml:61-62.
Evidence: codesearch dispatch 1792345312969-500-5ea0302066476f01 (npm install at doc-drift.yml:61, npm ci only in gh-pages.yml:43); codesearch dispatch 1792345319685-500-71b2ed35e296d80e (timeout-minutes present, npm audit at line 62 with --omit=dev --audit-level=high, no continue-on-error).
Acceptance: a live codesearch for `npm install --prefix gm-mcp` in .github returns zero hits, `npm ci --prefix gm-mcp` appears in doc-drift.yml, and a live codesearch for the lock drift shows the job fails on a package.json/lock mismatch.
material.subject: doc-drift uses npm install, so lockfile drift is never caught
material.witness: Commit 1cc112a52a8aac4c20c60f3c896eafb5613cafd0 (doc-drift.yml:64 npm install changed to npm ci --prefix gm-mcp, pushed to origin/main). Live codesearch dispatch 1792345843756-943-620015e1578990f4 found the old npm install line at line 64 before the edit; live codesearch dispatch 1792346001846-1057-64d4451d85b8ef4e finds the new npm ci line at doc-drift.yml:64 and the old literal 'npm install --prefix gm-mcp' returns 0 matches in .github. Job-level lock-drift failure is not witnessed locally; CI follow-up reads it.

material.acceptance_criteria: Witness: gh run view on a release run shows the selfcheck-admission-hold-reclaim step as its own job with a duration, and a failing selfcheck fails before the macOS x64 build job starts (or the job graph shows it parallel to build). A green release run cites its run id.
material.description: [repo: agentplug] [group: .github/workflows/release.yml] What is wrong: the release build job runs a selfcheck (selfcheck-admission-hold-reclaim) that exits 1 on macos-14 x86_64 and fails the whole release after the 60-minute build matrix finished. The failure is only visible at the end of the critical path, so each retry costs a full build cycle (release runs avg 163 s, max 263 s for the job set). Where: agentplug/.github/workflows/release.yml:59-81 (build matrix, timeout 60) and the selfcheck step in that job. Evidence: failed run 39123351941 (11:29, 'build (macos-14, x86_64-apple-darwin, agentplug-runner-macos-x64) selfcheck-admission-hold-reclaim exited 1'); 1 of 20 release runs failed. Lens: critical path and retry cost. Fix: move the selfcheck to a separate job that runs in parallel with the build matrix or ahead of it on the cheapest runner, and report its timing.
material.subject: agentplug release gates on a selfcheck that fails only on macOS x64

YAML parse confirms job set build, build-host-linux-arm64, bump, publish, selfcheck. Live codesearch at this dispatch shows the new job in the file. CI not awaited; the test follow-up reads CI for sha 029397fbc5e8.

material.description: [repo: rs-plugkit] [group: .github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml] Wrong: the 'Verify every uploaded asset is actually fetchable' step does one curl per asset and fails on the first non-200. GitHub release CDN propagation can lag right after upload, and skill-release.yml's equivalent step retries 5 times with sleep 5/10/15/20 seconds. The two release paths therefore disagree on the same guarantee. Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml, verify step (about line 150). Evidence: fs_read dispatches 1792345211523-500-19a23bc6096952a4 (wasm) and 1792345085282-500-b3682df759459df9 (skill-release). Fix: share one retry loop shape with skill-release.

material.acceptance_criteria: After a rerun on an existing release, `gh api repos/<repo>/releases/latest --jq .body` shows source-head equal to the newest bump commit and source-deps current; a following plan run with no source change logs 'no release' and skip=true. Witness: the two run ids.
material.description: [repo: rs-plugkit] [group: .github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml] Wrong: 'Publish release' creates the release with notes carrying source-head and source-deps only when `gh release view` fails. On a rerun where the release already exists it runs only `gh release upload --clobber`, so the body keeps the earlier source-head. The plan job compares that body with current main HEAD and deps; after a rerun that moved HEAD (the new bump commit) the skip check never matches, so each push re-bumps and re-releases. Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml, 'Publish release' step (about line 170) and the plan step's recorded_head sed (about line 45). Evidence: fs_read dispatch 1792345211523-500-19a23bc6096952a4. Fix: on an existing release, also update its notes (gh release edit --notes) with the current source-head and source-deps.
material.subject: wasm release rerun keeps stale source-head so plan never skips
material.witness: Publish release runs `gh release edit v$VER --notes $NOTES` in the existing-release else branch, so a rerun refreshes source-head/source-deps in the body. Live witness: exec_js 1792346448093-1282-b99177780222e106 parsed the workflow with PyYAML (11 release steps) and confirmed the edit in the Publish release run block. row.acceptance_criteria: After a rerun on an existing release, `gh api repos/<repo>/releases/latest --jq .body` shows source-head equal to the newest bump commit and source-deps current; a following plan run with no source change logs 'no release' and skip=true. Witness: the two run ids.
row.description: [repo: rs-plugkit] [group: .github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml] Wrong: 'Publish release' creates the release with notes carrying source-head and source-deps only when `gh release view` fails. On a rerun where the release already exists it runs only `gh release upload --clobber`, so the body keeps the earlier source-head. The plan job compares that body with current main HEAD and deps; after a rerun that moved HEAD (the new bump commit) the skip check never matches, so each push re-bumps and re-releases. Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml, 'Publish release' step (about line 170) and the plan step's recorded_head sed (about line 45). Evidence: fs_read dispatch 1792345211523-500-19a23bc6096952a4. Fix: on an existing release, also update its notes (gh release edit --notes) with the current source-head and source-deps.

material.description: Observed while landing 36ead6f8ab (AGENTS.md Dream-RSI probe rule). git_pull failed with 'Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: .gm/prd-log.jsonl' (dispatch 1792325568582-500-d2fb30cb09fbcc98). git_checkout on .gm/prd-log.jsonl was refused ('the project's own .gm/ and .agentplug* are never restored'), and git_stash with paths excluded .gm and saved nothing. Result: a runtime log that is tracked in git blocks every pull, so no local commit can reach origin. Fix direction: stop tracking .gm/prd-log.jsonl (or move it out of the tracked tree) so pull and push never depend on live spool state. Witness needed: git_pull on a tree with a dirty .gm/prd-log.jsonl returns ok:true.

material.acceptance_criteria: Witness: a push that changes src/ without a BUNDLE_VERSION bump produces exactly one failing job for the bump check (gh run view --json jobs lists one such job, not four) and the matrix jobs do not start. A push that bumps the version runs the matrix to green and cites its run id.
material.description: [repo: gm-mcp] [group: .github/workflows/verify.yml] What is wrong: verify.yml runs a 4-OS matrix (ubuntu, ubuntu-arm, macos, windows) for every push. The version-bump check (scripts/check-version-bump.mjs against github.event.before) is OS-independent and fails identically on all four legs, so one missing BUNDLE_VERSION bump costs four red legs and up to 170 s of runner time per push. The failing gate is 'a src/ change ships with a bumped BUNDLE_VERSION and a rebuilt bundle'. Where: gm-mcp/.github/workflows/verify.yml:28-62 (matrix at 31-34, bump step at 57-59). Evidence: 10 of 40 build-verify push runs failed; run 39135735174 (14:23) and run 39131583865 (13:26) failed on all four OS legs at the bump step (log lines cite that step on ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, windows-latest, macos-latest). Lens: CI critical path and job splitting. Fix: split the version-bump check into a single ubuntu job with no matrix, and gate the four-OS verify job on it with needs.
material.subject: gm-mcp build-verify runs the OS-independent version check 4 times
material.witness: Fix already on main in commit d4fa8fca ('verify: run version-bump check once, not per OS'): verify.yml has a single ubuntu version-bump job running scripts/check-version-bump.mjs against github.event.before, and the 4-OS verify matrix has needs: version-bump with an if that skips it on failure, so a bump failure starts no matrix leg. Live witness: exec_js confirmed d4fa8fca is an ancestor of HEAD 45b719ed; fs_read of verify.yml (dispatch 1792348361802-1272-8f6ac64ede54c03d) shows the split. CI on HEAD 45b719ed: run 39153415977 success, 5 jobs (1 bump + 4 verify legs), 0 failures.

Callers must either pass max_chars above 80 KB or re-read the whole list, costing tokens and CPU on every reconcile. material.acceptance_criteria: live dream-replay-cycle writes cycle-result.json with kind cycle-result and reply field cycle_result_path; codesearch literal replay_result_path in dream_cycle.rs returns 0
material.description: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/orchestrator/dream_rsi.rs:2161-2169 persist_replay_result(file,...) hardcodes "kind": "replay-result" for every file arg, so dream_cycle.rs:61-65 writes cycle-result.json with kind replay-result, and dream_cycle.rs:70 returns the cycle-result path under key replay_result_path. A consumer keying on kind or on the reply field cannot tell a cycle result from a manual dream-replay/dream-round result; the old name is the surviving path beside the new. Fix: derive kind from the file constant (REPLAY_RESULT_FILE vs CYCLE_RESULT_FILE), rename the cycle reply field to cycle_result_path, rename persist_replay_result to persist_result; if YAGNI-3 deletes replay-result.json entirely, delete REPLAY_RESULT_FILE + persist_sealed_replay together instead. Witness: codesearch 1792314780856-500-da23ec7f8361275f.

material.description: No finder covers the installed-skill surface: install.sh, install.ps1 and bin/gm-install.js link ~/.claude/skills/<name> and ~/.agents/skills/<name> to <checkout>/skills (junction on Windows, symlink elsewhere), copy and record the mode in .gm-skill-install-modes when no durable source exists, park displaced installs under .gm-skill-prelink/, and the daemon refresh_installed_skills re-fetches skills/manifest.sha256 every 300 s. Nothing checks that a fresh checkout reports no DRIFT from node bin/gm-install.js --check-skills, that a copy under a checkout is flagged, or that the MSYS mklink /J rule holds on Windows.

material.description: [repo: gm-mcp] [group: gm-mcp/src/verb-table.js] Case folding has two names. grep's body schema lists ignore_case (honored: dispatch 1792345233502-500-5f99b3a269a3240c matched FSM_VALIDATE case-insensitively) and case_insensitive (dispatch 1792345235314-500-8f4d41143580ca38). codesearch refuses ignore_case with "codesearch body has undeclared key ignore_case" (gm-mcp/src/codemode.js:143) and accepts only case_insensitive, so one intent gets verb-specific behaviour. grep also types about eight fields as any (help, include, detail, columns, regex, fixed_strings, fixedStrings, ignore_case, file_source), so their semantics are not declared. material.acceptance_criteria: lean-p4.md judge clause and dream-rsi SKILL.md Schedule state: per-criterion rubric, both-orderings rule, length excluded, one calibration pair per run when the judge shares the author's model, and the verdict's owner (row id or orchestrator).
material.description: skills/gm/prose/lean-p4.md:141: judge is a separate agent with a rubric and returns a verdict. Missing: rubric shape (per-criterion pass/fail with cited evidence, not a holistic score), position-bias control (judge both orderings when comparing two outputs; disagreement = no verdict), verbosity bias control (length is not a criterion), calibration (a known-good/known-bad pair the judge must classify correctly in the same run before its verdict counts, required when judge and author share a model), and an owner who acts on the verdict (FAGAN: a finding needs a named owner). dream-rsi runs on the smallest model (SKILL.md 'Schedule') with no calibration at all.
material.resolution: already-satisfied: clause present at HEAD, no edit required

material.acceptance_criteria: Observation writes are append-only (JSONL via fs.appendFileSync like fs_append) or CAS-verified per write; N parallel dispatches in one session yield N observation records.
material.description: observe_dispatch (dream_rsi.rs:979-1019) reads the whole observations.json, pushes one record, and rewrites it with crate::pkfs::write (pkfs.rs:66), with no CAS, lock or append. Plugkit runs 4 concurrent workers and one session issues parallel calls (gm_codemode Promise.all), so two in-flight dispatches of the same session_id race and the last writer drops the other's record. Event loss breaks the at-least-once delivery the cycle trigger and Part B witness check (skills/dream-rsi/SKILL.md step 4) depend on: a held dispatch id can be absent from observations.json. Contrast: the witness log and prd logs use append/CAS (rs-plugkit AGENTS.md APPEND_ONLY_PATH_SUFFIXES, cas_retry_write_verified).

material.acceptance_criteria: Two consecutive dispatches in one session against a stale bundle: the second reply carries no full restart block (a one-line pointer or nothing), and the first reply still carries it; witnessed by two dispatch ids.
material.description:
[repo: gm-mcp] [group: gm-mcp/src/bundle-drift.js]
What is wrong: once the served bundle differs from the installed bundle and bundle_reloadable is false, every dispatch reply carries the full stale block (bundle_stale, served and installed versions and shas, and a multi-clause restart sentence with a command). The same text repeats in each reply of a session, costing tokens with no new information after the first reply.
Where: gm-mcp/src/bundle-drift.js:144 (restart required notice text) and the reply assembly that appends it.
Evidence: codesearch dispatches 1792343588701-500-b0d50deae0a038c4 and 1792343589652-500-5d93ea4fd9fe3c0c and 1792343610635-500-e44169ecf0ecd28e each repeat the 0.2.128 to 0.2.129 block (about 400 chars plus 6 header keys).
Hypothesis to verify: the notice can be emitted once per session (or once per distinct sha pair) with a short pointer afterwards, without losing the restart instruction.
material.subject: bundle_stale notice repeats on every reply until a restart
material.witness: Pre-fix repro: codesearch 1792350299395-4667-bb2bcae6d2a4bde6 and 1792350305636-4674-99325392fce75450 in one session both carried the full bundle_stale YAML block. Fix in gm-mcp dispatch.js withStaleBundleNotice: the full block is emitted only when bundleStalenessAnnouncement returns a line (once per installed bundle); later replies carry one pointer line. Witness on the rebuilt bundle over stdio (GM_MCP_TRANSPORT=stdio, two gm_codemode calls in one process): first reply 1792350693134-4824-62085449b082a13 has the block and the notice line; second reply 1792350694183-4826-758c8cffdf692b7e has no block and only the pointer. Final-bundle re-witness: first 1792350915904-4904-95f37df7510d7e2f has the block, second 1792350916907-4905-5d9cf39f7f83d43c has only the pointer. Shipped in gm-mcp commits 8aaf1bd1eb and 3fce69a589 (version bump 0.2.137); CI run 39157943826 green (5/5).

material.acceptance_criteria: scans holds no ReadDir across ticks: each tick lists .gm/dream-rsi fresh (bounded) and resumes from a stored owner-name cursor, or visits all owners within budget; the cache-full branch is deleted.
material.description: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/dream_cycle.rs:34 scans: HashMap<PathBuf, ReadDir>, bounded by MAX_ROOT_SCANNERS=256 (line 16), retained between 15-min ticks (tick lines 337-408) so each root holds an open directory handle on .gm/dream-rsi until exhausted at 8 entries per batch. This is accidental state: an OS handle held across sleeps (on Windows an open directory handle blocks rename/delete of .gm/dream-rsi and its parent), a cache-full branch ("root cursor cache full", line 354) that silently skips roots, and an iterator whose snapshot goes stale as owners are added. The essential state is just which owner to visit next.

material.description: git_pull on /workspace/gm refuses with 'Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: .gm/prd-log.jsonl' because the runtime log is tracked in git, is staged+modified locally (23 appended lines), and origin/main also changed it. git_stash excludes .gm, and git_checkout refuses any .gm/ pathspec ('the project's own .gm/ and .agentplug* are never restored'), so no verb can clear it. Fix direction: untrack runtime logs (prd-log.jsonl, mutables-log.jsonl) or let git_pull merge them by union.

material.acceptance_criteria: Plan job fails or skips when gh api returns an error; no new patch version is pushed for an unchanged source and deps tuple.
material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: .github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml]
Wrong: the plan job reads the last release body with `gh api ... 2>/dev/null || true` (line 79). When auth fails or the API errors, recorded_head is empty, skip stays false, and the release job bumps the patch version and publishes again on every trigger, even when source and deps are unchanged.
Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/wasm-plugin-release.yml:79 (and the skip logic just below it).
Evidence: codesearch '|| true' dispatch 1792343631084-500-156065d48cdbce39 (line 79, column 88); fs_read dispatch 1792343617600-500-ed727f093e443b1f.
Acceptance: with the release API unreadable, the plan job exits non-zero or reports skip=true and no version bump commit is pushed; with a readable release whose source-head matches, skip=true is witnessed by a dispatch run.
material.subject: wasm release skip check masks gh api failure, releases every run
material.witness: Repro dispatch 1792352074898-1227-b4640ad0fffc97c (rs-plugkit cwd): gh api with a bad token exits 1 (HTTP 401) and the old '|| true' masked it, so the plan job read an empty body and skip stayed false. Fix in rs-plugkit commit 90bfd30de1 (on main as 1722857): the plan job exits 1 on any non-404 API error and treats only HTTP 404 (no release yet) as empty. Witness dispatch 1792352293443-5000-a1dd01b603403391: the new check with a bad token exits 1 with 'Bad credentials (HTTP 401)' and makes no release decision. CI for sha 17228570312357eb2fcebe2e3c8dadbe5f5d6239: run 39159504846 success, 9/9 jobs green.

material.acceptance_criteria: 1) A live dispatch that forces CAS contention on the subagent ledger (two concurrent subagent_start/subagent_end) completes with ok:true. 2) During the retry window the rs-plugkit wasm guest does not hold a core busy: sampled CPU of the runner process stays below one core while a retry is pending. 3) codesearch regex `while host_now_ms\(\) <` in subagent.rs returns zero hits.
material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/orchestrator/subagent.rs]

What is wrong: pause_ms (subagent.rs:164) waits by spinning `while host_now_ms() < until {}`, and append_event (subagent.rs:176) calls it with backoff_ms(attempt) on every CAS retry. Under contention each waiting subagent burns a full core for up to LEDGER_BACKOFF_CAP_MS per attempt, which is the CPU and thrash cost this lens targets.

Where: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/orchestrator/subagent.rs:164 and :176.

Evidence: codesearch regex pause_ms|append_event( on subagent.rs (dispatch 1792352637526-5000-8a007b155923da57) shows the spin at 164 and the call at 176; fs_read of 150-174 (dispatch 1792352629719-5000-2c146765488df843) shows the loop body.

Fix direction: give the wasm host a sleep verb or yield, or spread retries with the host clock poll replaced by a host sleep import; keep jitter_ms.
material.subject: wasm ledger backoff busy-spins the CPU instead of sleeping
material.witness: Commit dea7b3c2631e07b57e2a9a54d68c7e6bb25275f9 (6743b7addd, pushed to rs-plugkit main) replaces the busy-spin pause_ms in subagent.rs with a host_exec_js setTimeout sleep. Live subagent-start and subagent-end dispatches through the lifecycle handler returned ok:true. The CAS retry path that calls pause_ms was not forced under contention in this session, so the no-spin acceptance is witnessed by the wasm build and CI, not by this dispatch. Native cargo check -p rs-plugkit --offline passed. The wasm32 cfg block was not compiled locally because rs-search needs network under --offline.
