material.acceptance_criteria: 1) A live dispatch on a store lock whose owner file has only a pid line is reclaimed within STORE_LOCK_STALE_MS when that pid is dead, and reports reclaimed in the eprintln reason. 2) A live dispatch with a fresh owner file (pid alive, mtime recent) is still reported Held. 3) codesearch literal `ts > 0 &&` in claim_dispatch.rs returns zero hits after the fix.
material.description:
[repo: agentplug] [group: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon/claim_dispatch.rs]

What is wrong: read_store_lock_owner (claim_dispatch.rs, near line 700) defaults the timestamp to 0 when the owner file's second line is missing or unparsable. owner_record_is_stale (line 698-700) returns `ts > 0 && ...`, so a ts of 0 is never stale by age. A lock whose owner file lacks a timestamp is reclaimed only if the separate pid-liveness path fires; if that path also reads the pid as live (pid reuse, or a foreign host sharing the .gm dir), the store lock stays held with no age-based escape.

Where: agentplug/crates/agentplug-runner/src/daemon/claim_dispatch.rs:698-700 and the read at the same file near line 700.

Evidence: fs_read of claim_dispatch.rs 690-719 (dispatch 1792352616009-5000-72e9c8be6a1acd37) and 730-769 (dispatch 1792352643183-5000-fd88f4833f741ac1) show the ts=0 default and the reclaim path. Unverified live: no dispatch yet reproduces a held lock with a ts-less owner file; the first step is to witness that before editing.

Fix direction: treat a missing or unparsable timestamp as age measured from the owner file mtime (stamp_age_ms already accepts a path), so every owner record can age out.
material.subject: Store lock owner with no timestamp is never aged out
material.witness: claim_dispatch.rs owner_record_is_stale now reads stamp_age_ms(ts, owner_file) >= STORE_LOCK_STALE_MS (line 699); the live exec_js reads the edited source and confirms the 'ts > 0 &&' guard is absent. Pushed 42737a585be579acd6ec82f1e24b26bd5113faa0 to main (git_push dispatch 1792352992914-970-b778615de34f0078). Dead-pid reclaim behavior needs a rebuilt runner and is not witnessed live here.

material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/native-check.yml]
What is wrong: default-features, slim-features and unit-tests are three separate ubuntu jobs. Each restores its own rust-cache key (native-check-default, native-check-default, native-check-unit-tests) and each runs its own cold-ish cargo build of the same crate on the same toolchain, so the dependency graph is compiled up to three times per push. Only the default and slim jobs differ in features; the unit-tests job differs only in cargo subcommand. The unit-tests job also does not wait on the check jobs, so a failing check still spends a full test build.
Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/native-check.yml lines 31-66 (the three job blocks and their cache keys).
Evidence: native-check runs on rs-plugkit main: 39160104247 (19:44:01 to 19:44:50, about 49 s), 39159727500 (about 49 s), 39159504866 (about 112 s), 39159178717 (about 40 s). Those are the three-job totals per push; the per-job split was not pulled in this session (`gh run view <id> --json jobs`).
acceptance_criteria: one ubuntu job runs cargo check (default and slim) and cargo test against one shared cache key, or the test job declares needs on the check job; gh run view --json jobs for the next push shows total ubuntu compile time below the sum of the current three jobs.
material.subject: native-check compiles rs-plugkit three times across jobs
material.witness: Commit 8ff6bc58f6 (ci: share native-check cache, gate unit tests) pushed to rs-plugkit main at 5a42338e421b (git_push from rs-plugkit lists 8ff6bc58f6; dispatch 1792353046147-1374-f59a2f25163ab55d). Witness dispatch fs_read of rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/native-check.yml shows unit-tests needs default-features and key native-check-default on all three jobs. CI not awaited per row instructions.

row.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/native-check.yml]
What is wrong: default-features, slim-features and unit-tests are three separate ubuntu jobs. Each restores its own rust-cache key (native-check-default, native-check-default, native-check-unit-tests) and each runs its own cold-ish cargo build of the same crate on the same toolchain, so the dependency graph is compiled up to three times per push. Only the default and slim jobs differ in features; the unit-tests job differs only in cargo subcommand. The unit-tests job also does not wait on the check jobs, so a failing check still spends a full test build.
Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/native-check.yml lines 31-66 (the three job blocks and their cache keys).
Evidence: native-check runs on rs-plugkit main: 39160104247 (19:44:01 to 19:44:50, about 49 s), 39159727500 (about 49 s), 39159504866 (about 112 s), 39159178717 (about 40 s). Those are the three-job totals per push; the per-job split was not pulled in this session (`gh run view <id> --json jobs`).
acceptance_criteria: one ubuntu job runs cargo check (default and slim) and cargo test against one shared cache key, or the test job declares needs on the check job; gh run view --json jobs for the next push shows total ubuntu compile time below the sum of the current three jobs.

material.acceptance_criteria: persist_replay_result signature takes no `Value` and no bare `file: &str`; identity keys cannot be overwritten (insert-after-extend visible in source); callers compile unchanged in behavior.
material.description: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/orchestrator/dream_rsi.rs:2161-2174: record = {kind:"replay-result", source, owner_session_id, ts}; then target.extend(extra) lets any caller key replace the identity fields the cycle-result reader relies on, and the if-let on Value::Object drops a non-object fields with no error. Two same-typed &str params (file, source) are swappable at call sites (2205, dream_cycle.rs:61 path). Return Option<String> loses why a write failed. The signature is more general than the contract. Narrow to fields: serde_json::Map (or a typed ReplaySummary), insert identity keys after extend (or refuse collisions), take file as a ReplayResultFile enum/const newtype, and return Result<String, PersistError>.
material.resolution: Fix already at rs-plugkit HEAD 240036850896 (dream_rsi.rs clean in working tree): persist_replay_result takes ReplayFile enum, ReplaySource newtype and serde_json::Map; identity keys inserted after caller fields. No gm-repo edit needed, so no gm push.

material.acceptance_criteria: a gh run log of predicates-md-drift shows a rust-cache restore before the cargo step, and a second run on unchanged Cargo.lock finishes its generate step in under half the cold-run time
material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/predicates-md-drift.yml]
What is wrong: the check-drift job runs `cargo run -q -p rs-plugkit --example predicates_md` after dtolnay/rust-toolchain but with no Swatinem/rust-cache step, so every push or PR touching predicate_registry.rs compiles the whole rs-plugkit dependency graph from scratch. The sibling workflows native-check.yml and rust-ci.yml (agentplug) both restore a rust-cache.
Where: rs-plugkit/.github/workflows/predicates-md-drift.yml (the 'generate predicates.md' step; no cache step precedes it).
Evidence: workflow file read in dispatch 1792352683453-5000-b6956d158e169c94 is the process-leak file, and the predicates-md-drift file read in the same session; native-check runs on rs-plugkit main with cache (gh run 39160104247, ~49 s). The predicates-md-drift run ids were not captured in this session; pull them with `gh run list -R AnEntrypoint/rs-plugkit --workflow predicates-md-drift.yml`.
acceptance_criteria: a live dispatch or gh run log of predicates-md-drift shows a rust-cache restore line before the cargo step, and a second run on an unchanged Cargo.lock finishes its generate step in under half the cold-run time.
material.subject: predicates-md-drift builds rs-plugkit cold on every run (no rust-cache)
material.witness: Commit 33bb665e21391dcf0e92fe4d48fc8e20d553e5a7 (ci: cache cargo build in predicates-md-drift) adds Swatinem/rust-cache@63fed3e2fecf6f7b51dc6f043341b79ef82a9ae7 (the pin native-check.yml uses) with workspaces: rs-plugkit before the generate step. Live fs_read of the edited file shows the step; the staged-secrets check printed RESULT: PASS; the commit is on origin/main (git_push reported remote 5a42338 containing it). CI cache-hit timing is not claimed here.

material.acceptance_criteria: A live fs_read of rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/Cargo.toml shows the rs-search git dependency carries rev or tag equal to the sha in rs-plugkit/Cargo.lock; a live dispatch of `cargo metadata --locked` in rs-plugkit (via bash verb) exits 0 and reports rs-search source at that same sha.
material.description:
[repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/Cargo.toml]
What is wrong: the wasm32 dependency rs-search is declared as git = "https://github.com/AnEntrypoint/rs-search.git" with no rev, tag or branch. Cargo.lock pins it to 1bbeaf68c953e665979c2f8c9b69550599c0827e, but any lock regeneration or `cargo update -p rs-search` moves it to the remote default branch tip with no review, so the wasm build can change without a manifest diff.
Where: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/Cargo.toml (target.'cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")'.dependencies, rs-search line); rs-plugkit/Cargo.lock:843-845 (source pinned to 1bbeaf68).
Evidence: fs_read of rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/Cargo.toml (find-12-1018 session, dispatch ids in exec-spool); grep literal `rs-search` in rs-plugkit/Cargo.lock returned 3 hits at lines 833, 843, 845 (dispatch 1792352755629-5000-5de106d5c7de07f2 family).
material.subject: rs-search git dep has no rev or tag in rs-plugkit manifest
material.witness: Cargo.toml rs-search dep pins rev=1bbeaf68c953e665979c2f8c9b69550599c0827e, the Cargo.lock sha and remote main tip (api.github.com commits/main, dispatch 1792353054125-5000-d0155849349deafe). Cargo.lock updated for the rev source line and rs-plugkit version sync. cargo metadata --locked exits 0 and reports rs-search source git+https://github.com/AnEntrypoint/rs-search.git?rev=1bbeaf68...#1bbeaf68.... Committed 7d3a512e1adb1169dc43b66ae6de7cb3ddf52923 on main, pushed to origin.

material.acceptance_criteria: A live codesearch {query:"TODO", mode:"comments", path:"gm-mcp/src"} either reads every JS file in that subtree (files_scanned equals the JS file count) or lists in paths_not_read only files with no comment syntax, each with its reason.
material.description: [repo: rs-plugkit] [group: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/code_index.rs] What is wrong (PLAUSIBLE, not yet confirmed against the language filter): codesearch mode comments with path gm-mcp/src on the query TODO reports files_scanned:5 of 43 tracked files, paths_not_read_count:38, exhaustive:false, and the reply gives no per-path reason. JS sources in that subtree carry comments, so the scan may skip files it should read. Where: rs-plugkit/crates/plugkit-core/src/code_index.rs (paths_not_read). Evidence: dispatch 1792352677293-5000-917212d745325395. Related: the unscoped scan in dispatch 1792352657601-5000-2a03edd2d139a830 has the same non-exhaustive flag.
material.subject: Comments-mode scan reads 5 of 43 files without a stated reason
material.witness: Commit f81f1ab3657431a23525c8d7c79c604aa034578f (rs-plugkit main) adds paths_not_read_reason and names the cap on paths_not_read_note. cargo check -p rs-plugkit --offline passes. Live codesearch comments gm-mcp/src with k:1 hits the cap (files_scanned 5, paths_not_read_count 38) and the served wasm still returns the old note, since the new build ships through CI. The default scan reads files_scanned 43 with no cap, so the pre-edit reason is the matches cap.

Witness dispatches: pull 1792328999374-500-f38b3ee15d290cd6, push 1792329000278-500-98b6ff77cca7db2c. Fix needed: git_pull or git_push should isolate foreign dirty overlap (or refuse with the lane owner named) rather than leave the commit unpushed.
